source: a true 3D room-decorating game (not a 2D, top-down, or UI/screen-based game): the player stands in a 3D room in third person and furnishes it by picking real furniture and props (such as a sofa, table, chair, lamp, plant, or rug) from an in-game catalog/menu and placing them into the room. Each furniture item must be a recognizable, real 3D furniture MODEL sourced from the Roblox asset library / Toolbox (search for the asset and insert the model), not a plain recolored box or a 2D image. Include a goal such as filling a set of placement slots or reaching a completion meter, and make sure placed items rest on the floor. The room and furniture must exist as 3D world objects with depth, not as a 2D/GUI layout. Do not ask any clarifying questions. Make any reasonable creative decisions yourself and build the complete, playable game now.

answers.ask: No style is stated beyond real furniture - should the room read as a contemporary apartment, a cosy cottage, or a bright stylised showroom?
answers.answer: Use a contemporary apartment style with a simple, believable furnished-room look.

answers.ask: Is the completion meter filled by using every slot, or by some scoring of what was placed?
answers.answer: Fill the completion meter by placing furniture into every designated placement slot; no additional scoring is needed.

answers.ask: One room only, or does the room open onto more rooms once it is filled?
answers.answer: Build one room only as a complete, playable decorating space.

scene_prompt: Create a true 3D third-person room-decorating map set in one contemporary apartment room. Build a believable enclosed room with floor, walls, ceiling, doorway, and windows, leaving open floor areas for furniture placement. Arrange designated floor-level placement slots around the room for recognizable 3D furniture models such as a sofa, table, chairs, lamps, plants, and rugs; placed items rest naturally on the floor. Frame the room as a complete playable decorating space with a clear view across the interior.

## Genre

Simulation is the sole genre. The author describes a task-focused 3D furnishing simulator whose completion meter advances as designated slots are filled.

## Shape and preset

Use `interior-single`, taken from outside Simulation’s usual shapes because the complete map is one enclosed apartment room and the player never crosses to an exterior. Preset is none: Simulation’s Sandbox preset assumes independent outdoor plots and resource collection, so it is not recognisable after adapting it to this room.

## Config requirements

Draw a believable contemporary apartment interior with a floor, four walls, ceiling, doorway, and windows. Preserve generous empty floor areas for furnishing. Draw the visible half of `trigger-task` as understated placement-slot outlines suitable for sofas, a table, chairs, lamps, plants, and rugs. Any example furniture shown must be recognizable, fully modeled 3D assets with realistic depth and floor contact, never flat images or primitive placeholder boxes.

## Layout requirements

Place one functional `trigger-task` at every designated furnishing slot, matching the generated slot count; the prompt gives no exact quantity. Distribute slots by furniture footprint: sofa against a long wall, table and chair slots grouped without overlap, lamps beside seating, plants near windows or corners, and rugs flat beneath open seating arrangements. All slots must be walkable from the doorway and filling every slot must be possible without blocking access to another.

## Layout components

The build is one enclosed, level-floored apartment room with a single doorway and exterior-facing windows. An open circulation path runs from the doorway across the center and branches to every furnishing area. Placement areas occupy the perimeter and selected central floor patches while maintaining believable clearances. Props comprise recognizable sofa, table, chair, lamp, plant, and rug models in quantities determined by the slot layout. The walls and ceiling bound the play space. Compose the view from an elevated cutaway corner with an unobstructed read across the whole interior.

## Render order

Use `isometric`: render the authoritative room composition first, then derive its top-down placement plan, because spatial presentation and furniture readability lead.

## Scale, theme, and pipeline cost

Scale is small, fixed to one playable room. Theme is simple, believable contemporary apartment. Use `P0`; the room is a single unstacked interior with no outside transition.
